newsitem.title: USA: Galileo sees loss for fiscal 1997.
newsitem.headline: Galileo sees loss for fiscal 1997.

text.p: Galileo Corp said Tuesday that it is likely to report a loss for fiscal 1997, ended September 30, as a result of a substantial loss of business with Xerox Corp, its largest customer.

The company said it received written notification from Xerox that it had developed internal production capabilities for dicorotron assemblies and would no longer purchase these assemblies from Galileo.

These assemblies accounted for approximately $20,400,000, or 48 percent, of Galileo's fiscal 1996 revenues and approximately $2,700,000, or 34 percent, of Galileo's second quarter fiscal 1997 revenues, respectively.

As previously reported, the company said it has adopted a reorganization plan in response to the loss of Xerox. In connection with that plan, the company recorded a non-recurring charge of $6,872,000, or $1.01 per share in the second quarter, resulting in a loss of $7,378,000, or $1.08 per share.
The company said, however, that it believes its reorganization plan along with significant cash balances, will allow it to return to profitability by the first calendar quarter of 1998.
